summary: Tested the separate auth_credentials store, branding and the migration PDF. DB: users has 0 docs with password_hash, auth_credentials has exactly one doc per user (10 of 10), the unique index on user_id exists, and every hash starts with $2b$. API: SuperAdmin login works. A TEST employee can log in, a wrong password gives 401, and 5 failures give 429 (also via the email alias, because the canonical user:<id> key is used). No response leaks password_hash. Change-password, admin reset, employee edit with a password, credential slip (TEST employee only) and staff create/update with a password all write to auth_credentials: each new password works and the old one fails. A staff update without a password keeps the existing one. Vendor sync was run once: status success (9 updated, 0 created). A before/after snapshot of auth_credentials (updated_at and hash) showed 0 changes. Manifest name and short_name are correct. The PDF is 5 pages, mentions emp.arunenterprisespryg.in 6 times and hr. 0 times. UI: SuperAdmin login reaches /admin, a wrong password shows 'Invalid ...', and the TEST employee reaches /employee on mobile. Found 2 backend bugs and 1 environment issue (title).

critical.issue: The auth_credentials doc is NOT deleted, so an orphan bcrypt hash is left behind. Reproduced 5 times; the orphans created by testing were removed manually by id. Fix: await db.auth_credentials.delete_one({'user_id': emp_id/uid}) in both delete routes (a delete_credentials helper in credentials.py would be cleaner).

minor.issue: The reset does not clear the lockout. The login key is now f'user:{_id}', but reset deletes identifiers [email, employee_id.lower()], so a locked-out employee still gets 429 with the new password for 15 minutes. Fix: delete {'identifier': f"user:{doc['_id']}"} as well. The credential-slip route also does not clear login_attempts.

ui_bugs.issue: The served HTML still had the old '<title>ARUN ENTERPRISES | Employee Portal' because the CRA dev server does not hot-reload public/index.html. Fixed by restarting the frontend with supervisor. The title is now 'ARUN ENTERPRISES EMP PORTAL'. The production build will pick it up anyway.

action_items: Delete the auth_credentials doc when an employee or staff user is deleted
In reset-password (and credential-slips), clear login_attempts with identifier f'user:{_id}'
critical_code_review_comments: vendor_sync._upsert_one now only $sets profile fields on users; set_password is used only for newly created employees. Credentials are isolated (verified).
run_sync still receives the unused hash_password argument; it can be removed
change-password does not end the user's other sessions, while staff password changes do (inconsistent)
The startup seed resets the admin password from .env whenever password_set_in_app is not set and the password differs (pre-existing behaviour)
server.py is about 1600 lines; split it into routers

success_rate.backend: 92% (11/12 in the suite; the failing one is the real reset-clears-lockout bug), plus 1 bug found in the delete cleanup DB check

seed_data_creation: Created TEST_CR<run> employees, TEST_CRUI1 and test_crstaff<run>@example.com staff users; all deleted. Their orphan auth_credentials docs and login_attempts were removed by id. Final state: users 10, auth_credentials 10, 0 orphans, 0 TEST users. No real employee or SuperAdmin credential was changed (snapshot diff empty).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run: pytest tests/test_auth_credentials_store.py -n 0. After it runs, the delete routes leave orphan auth_credentials docs until the bug is fixed (test_db_no_password_hash_in_users compares the users count with the creds count). The vendor sync was run once in this iteration; do not repeat it unnecessarily.
